 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SANDEEP N. BHATT  Date : 13/09/2024  COMMON ORAL JUDGMENT NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2462/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined 1.

The present First Appeals, under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, are preferred by the appellant- insurance company of the offending tempo, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned common judgment and award dated 29.11.2006 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, (Aux.) Vadodara in Motor Accident Claims Petition Nos.1924 of 1993, 371 of 1994, 372 of 1994 respectively, by which the learned Tribunal has awarded compensation to the claimants as stated in the impugned judgment and award to the claimant/s, holding all the opponents jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 2. As common question of facts and law are involved in the appeals, with the consent of learned advocates for the parties, all these appeals are disposed of by this common judgment.
The parties are referred to as per their original status before the learned Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
3.1 The claimants filed the claim petitions stating that on 24.10.1993 at about 5.00 a.m., the injured as well as the deceased were travelling in a vehicle bearing No.GJ.7U.7607 NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2462/2007 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/09/2024 undefined and when they reached near Kandari, one truck bearing registration no.UP-7B-1776 was parked on the main tar road rashly and negligent and without observing traffic rules and regulations and without any signal, backlight or reflector so as to warn the vehicles coming on the road and as it was early hours, the tempo driver dashed with the truck from behind and therefore the accident occurred.
Therefore, the claimants filed the claim petitions claiming compensation.
3.2 Upon service of notice to the opponents, the opponents field the written statements denying the contents of the claim petitions.
Thereafter, the learned Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.

After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petitions by awarding compensation as mentioned in the impugned judgment and award.
3.3 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and awards passed by the Tribunal, the present appeals are preferred by the insurance company.

sentences.text: 4. Heard learned advocates for the parties.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2462/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined 4.1
The impugned judgment and award is assailed mainly on the ground of negligence.

Learned advocate for the appellant-insurance company has submitted that the learned Tribunal has erred in attributing the negligence on the part of the tempo at 65% and on the part of the truck at 35% as, the accident has solely occurred due to the fact that the truck was parked in the middle of the road without any signal or light.
The learned Tribunal ought to have held the truck more negligent for the accident.

She also argued that as the claimants/injured were illegal passengers in the goods vehicle, their risk is not covered by the policy and therefore also, whatever negligence is attributed between the two vehicles, the appellant-insurance company ought to have been exonerated from payment of compensation.
She, therefore, prayed to allow these appeals.

4.2 Learned advocate appearing for the insurance company of the offending truck has submitted that when the offending truck was coming from Bombay side towards Baroda on national highway no.8 near Kandari village, the said truck became defective and the driver stopped it at the side of the road and parked it leaving more than sufficient space for the other vehicle by keeping the lights on and the tempo driver was driving his tempo so fast that he could not control the steering and banged with the rear side of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2462/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined truck causing the accident.

He, therefore, submitted that it is the tempo driver who is solely negligent for the accident and even if the contributory negligence on the part of the truck driver is accepted, then the negligence apportioned to the truck of 35% is also on the higher side and it should be reduced to a minimum.
In any case, the negligence of the truck cannot be increased as the tempo driver was negligent for the accident.
He, therefore, prayed to dismiss these appeals.
5. I have considered the submissions made by the respective parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
I have also considered the pleadings of the parties before the Tribunal.
6. The issue which is required to be considered is of the contributory negligence.

It transpires from the FIR, panchanama and depositions of witnesses that the eye witness-Shankuntalaben who is one of the claimants has deposed on oath and stated that she along with her brother's son were travelling in eicher tempo and when she reached near Kandari village on N.H.No.8, one truck was standing and there is no light or reflector nor any stone and the vehicles coming from the opposite direction with full head NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2462/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined light and due to this the driver of the tempo could not see the standing truck and hence it dashed with the truck.
The driver of the eicher tempo also deposed and stated the same facts.
The offending driver was also examined who was also an eye-witness to the incident, however, he stated contrary facts.
In this background, if the FIR and panchanama of the place of incident are seen, it is clear that the tempo dashed with the stationary truck from behind.
The truck is in stationary condition due to some default, without any head- light on or any other mark to indicate the other vehicles coming on the road that the truck is standing.
Further, the tempo driver was coming in his own speed and dashed with the truck from behind.

In this case, had the truck driver took extra care to put more indicators to know the other vehicles that the truck is standing on the road, the accident Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Aliahmad Mohammad Ali Banzara on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45489800/
3 could have been avoided.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Had the tempo driver was in a moderate speed and not in full speed, he could have controlled his tempo and stopped it even though he could have seen the truck in the last minute.
But, it seems that due to the speed, he did not get that chance to stop the vehicle and it dashed with the truck.
This accident has happened due to no extra care and caution of both the vehicles.

Therefore, in the opinion of this Court, both the vehicles are equally negligent for the accident and therefore I apportion the negligence between the tempo and truck at NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2462/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined 50% -50%.

7. On the submission made by the appellant that the tempo driver was not having valid licence, it seems that it was a mere statement made by the insurance company, and nothing is produced to prove the same and therefore, in view of the recent judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court, mere bald statements cannot be considered and they should be supported by evidence.
8.

In the case of Vilasbhai Thore v. Shivabhai Tejabhai Harijan reported in 2014(3) GLR 2025 , the coordinate Bench of this court has held in paragraphs 4 to 6 as under:
4.

sentences.text:
The issue of negligence decided by the Tribunal, reads as under:
"So far as the question of negligence is concerned, Pankajbhai Ramanlal Shah,
petitioner of MACP No. 1432/96 is examined at Exh. 37.
Deepakkumar Keshavlal Bhavsar, petitioner of MACP No. 1431/96 is examined at Exh. 55 and Vilasbhai Thore, petitioner of MACP No. 1414/96 is examined at Exh.72.

Reiterating the contents they have stated in their deposition, inter alia, that on 26.10.1996 at about 5.50 p.m. They were travelling in a NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2462/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined Maruti Car bearing registration No.
GJ-1-PP-2516 while going from Ahmedabvad to Nadiad.
It was being driven by Opponent No. 4 of MACP No. 1431/96 and 1432/96 Vilasbhai Thore on the left hand side of the road at a moderate speed.
Near Kheda camp on the highway, one truck bearing registration No. GJ-3T-3279 came from the opposite direction to a great speed and collided with the jeep.
The petitioners sustained injuries.
All the petitioners have been cross-examined at length on behalf of the insurance company.
It transpires from their cross- examination that the collision between the two vehicles took place when Maruti Car was climbing a slope of river Shedi.
Over and above the oral evidence, the petitioners have produced a copy of complaint at Exh.39, a copy of the panchnama at Exh. 39.
From the oral as well as the documentary evidence, it is abundantly clear that the collision between the two vehicles took place when the car was climbing the slope of river Shedi.

It is a fact that when there is a slope on a bridge or a culvert and if two vehicles are coming from the opposite directions, one cannot see the vehicle coming unless the coming vehicles comes at the top of the slope or the vehicle wherein one is travelling reaches to the top because, on both the sides of the bridge there is a slope.

It is therefore, advisable that NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2462/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined the vehicles coming from both the directions should drive their respective vehicles in the extreme left hand side and should reduce the speed unless the rad ahead is totally visible.

4 accident appears to have taken place because the drivers of both the vehicles did not take their respective vehicles on the extreme left hand side nor reduced the speed.

sentences.text: The driver of the truck could not seen Maruti Car coming from the opposite direction nor the driver of the Maruti Car could see the driver of the truck on the other side because of the slope.
Suddenly when they saw the other vehicle, it was too late and the drivers could not control their respective vehicles because of their speed and that is how the collision took place.
In my opinion, therefore.it is a case of contributory negligence and it appears to be a head-on-collision and, therefore, the drivers of both the vehicles are equally responsible for the accident.

I, therefore, attribute 50%
negligence to the drivers of both the vehicles.
Exh. 40 is a copy of the policy of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.
It shows that at the relevant time, the opponent No. 2 was the owner and opponent No. 3 was the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Exh. 41 is a certificate of insurance issued by opponent No. 6 United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. which shows that at the relevant time, the opponent No. 5 was the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2462/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined owner and opponent No. 6 was the insurer of the Maruti Car in question.
Thus, all the opponents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
In MACP No. 1414/96 the driver of the Maruti Car himself is the petitioner and, therefore, the owner and insurer of the said vehicle have not been joined as opponents.

I, therefore,
decide issue No. 1 accordingly."
5. This is one of the bone of the contention that the Tribunal has, not considered the fact that there were two vehicles of unequivalent magnitude involved in the accident.
6. The concept of contributory negligence requires to be considered in this case.
The vehicles were not of equal magnitude.

It was an involvement of truck of one side which was coming down of the slope and there were marks of brakes of car, and therefore it can be said that the driver of the car had taken pre-caution, whereas the driver of the truck lost the control and collusion took place.
The contributory negligence of small vehicle is less compare to a big vehicle.
The driver of the big vehicle has to take more caution.

In light of the facts and circumstances as emerges before this Court, the driver of the truck was more negligent than the driver of the car, and therefore, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2462/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined the negligence of driver of the car can be attributed to 30% instead of 50%."
Therefore, in view of the above discussion, I am of the view that these appeals are required to be allowed partly.
9. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.

9.1 The present appeals are partly allowed to the extent that the judgment and award dated 29.11.2006 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, (Aux.) Vadodara in Motor Accident Claims Petition Nos.1924 of 1993, 371 of 1994, 372 of 1994 respectively, is modified to the extent that the opponent nos.1 to 3 and opponent nos.4 to 6 are liable to pay the compensation at 50%-
50%.
